prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. For $x,y\in A$, write $R(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in R$. Which condition defines reflexivity?

answers.explanation: Every element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted.
No element has a self-loop; pairs of different elements are unrestricted. This defines irreflexivity, not reflexivity.
Every related pair has its reverse; loops are allowed but not required. This defines symmetry, not reflexivity.

answers.text: $\forall x\in A\;\forall y\in A\;\forall z\in A\; ((R(x,y)\land R(y,z))\Rightarrow R(x,z))$.
answers.explanation: Every two-step chain has its direct shortcut, including chains with repeated vertices. This defines transitivity, not reflexivity.
Only one element needs to relate to itself. This defines existence of a self-loop, not reflexivity.
Each element has at least one outgoing related element, which may be itself. This defines seriality, not reflexivity.
All diagonal pairs and no off-diagonal pairs are present. This defines equality as the entire relation, not reflexivity.
Every pair is comparable, including an element with itself, so all loops are required. This defines comparability including equal elements, not reflexivity.
Every ordered pair is present, including every loop. This defines universality, not reflexivity.
Every related pair is diagonal; some or all loops may be missing. This defines coreflexivity, not reflexivity.
